scoring: Account IQ = ICP fit (30) + trigger strength (30) + operational complexity (25) + reachability (15). Public signals are research candidates only, not qualified opportunities or claims of current ERP need.

accounts.why_now: Two businesses were acquired simultaneously in a carve-out to create a new specialty-chemicals platform.
accounts.hypothesis: A newly formed platform may need to rationalize finance, inventory, intercompany, reporting and standalone systems as it separates from prior ownership.
accounts.first_move: Lead with TSA / separation readiness and multi-entity finance architecture, not a generic NetSuite demo.
accounts.buyers: CFO, Controller, PE Operating Partner, IT / Operations
accounts.gaps: Current ERP, separation deadlines, entity structure, inventory complexity, existing advisory relationships.

accounts.why_now: Saothair Capital completed the acquisition of FIFCO USA and returned the business to the North American Breweries name under new ownership and a new CEO.
accounts.hypothesis: New PE ownership creates a natural window to review standalone systems, finance controls, supply chain, manufacturing and reporting requirements.
accounts.first_move: Use Baker Tilly food-and-beverage NetSuite proof plus a separation / modernization discovery with finance and operations.
accounts.buyers: CFO, Controller, Operations, IT, PE sponsor
accounts.gaps: ERP ownership post-transaction, TSA terms, current manufacturing stack, entity count, NetSuite/Oracle relationship.

accounts.why_now: Incline Equity Partners invested in the value-added industrial distribution and service provider, with stated plans to expand organically and through M&A.
accounts.hypothesis: Growth through add-ons can strain inventory, purchasing, entity reporting and field-service finance processes, creating an ERP standardization window.
accounts.first_move: Open with acquisition scalability, inventory visibility and finance close rather than software features.
accounts.buyers: CFO, Controller, Operations, PE sponsor, IT
accounts.gaps: Current ERP/WMS, acquisition roadmap, warehouse count, reporting pain, sponsor technology agenda.

accounts.why_now: Closed a $75M Series C in September 2026, bringing total funding to $223M while advancing a clinical-stage pipeline and expanding its platform.
accounts.hypothesis: Clinical-stage growth can create audit-readiness, procurement-control, multi-entity, grant / R&D spend and finance-scaling needs consistent with Baker Tilly life-sciences NetSuite work.
accounts.first_move: Research finance leadership and current ERP, then offer an IPO / clinical-stage controls readiness conversation.
accounts.gaps: Current finance stack, audit requirements, international entities, procurement controls, IPO timing.

accounts.why_now: Announced an oversubscribed $92.5M Series E to advance its oncology program into clinical development.
accounts.hypothesis: A later-stage financing round and transition into clinical development can increase SOX, procurement, reporting and investor-readiness requirements.
accounts.first_move: Use Baker Tilly's life-sciences NetSuite case study to frame finance controls and scalable procurement, not ERP replacement alone.
accounts.gaps: Current ERP, headcount, public-market plans, purchasing workflow, segregation-of-duties maturity.

accounts.why_now: Expanded its Series A financing to $80.5M while advancing a global Phase 2b program.
accounts.hypothesis: Global clinical operations plus new financing can create finance, procurement, entity and audit-control requirements before the organization becomes much larger.
accounts.first_move: Research controller/CFO structure and current system limits, then lead with scale-ready controls and multi-entity readiness.
accounts.buyers: Finance lead, Controller, Clinical Ops, IT
accounts.gaps: ERP status, entity count, clinical vendor spend, global subsidiaries, audit requirements.

accounts.why_now: Closed a $116M Series A to fund a pivotal Phase 2 study and expand its therapy pipeline.
accounts.hypothesis: Large early financing and multi-site clinical growth may outgrow entry-level finance processes quickly, especially procurement, grant / R&D spend and controls.
accounts.first_move: Map finance leadership and audit posture; position Baker Tilly as finance-process advisor before leading with NetSuite.
accounts.gaps: Current ERP, audit firm, entity structure, procurement volume, expected headcount growth.

accounts.why_now: Raised a $50M Series B at a $750M valuation in September 2026 while expanding an AI platform used in hardware programs.
accounts.hypothesis: Rapid SaaS growth can create ASC 606, multi-entity, billing, board-reporting and audit-readiness complexity before finance systems catch up.
accounts.first_move: Look for subscription-billing, close-cycle and entity-growth pain; use a CFO-level business case rather than generic ERP outreach.
accounts.gaps: Current accounting stack, billing model, entity count, close time, audit / IPO plans.

accounts.why_now: Raised $140M Series C to advance AI-designed therapeutics and expand pharmaceutical partnerships.
accounts.hypothesis: Large financing plus international operations can create multi-currency, entity consolidation, procurement and investor-reporting needs.
accounts.first_move: Confirm U.S. finance ownership and entity architecture, then position OneWorld / controls only if the platform fits.
accounts.gaps: Headquarters/ERP ownership, U.S. entities, current finance stack, audit needs, billing model.

accounts.why_now: Appointed Mark Johnson as CFO effective October 1, 2026, bringing finance leadership from large consumer and PE-backed businesses.
accounts.hypothesis: A new CFO often opens a 90-day window to reassess reporting, planning, inventory and operating systems, especially in growth-focused consumer brands.
accounts.first_move: Congratulate the CFO and ask about finance transformation priorities, inventory visibility and close/reporting friction before mentioning NetSuite.
accounts.gaps: Current ERP, inventory stack, close cycle, e-commerce integrations, transformation mandate.

accounts.why_now: Closed a $50M Series B led by Lockheed Martin to scale production and deployment amid rising demand.
accounts.hypothesis: Production scaling can expose inventory, procurement, project accounting, multi-entity and financial-control gaps.
accounts.first_move: Research current manufacturing/finance stack and lead with scaling controls, inventory and project visibility.
accounts.gaps: ERP/MRP stack, government-contracting requirements, inventory model, entity count, Oracle conflicts.

accounts.why_now: Announced a comprehensive recapitalization to strengthen the balance sheet and fund organic and inorganic growth.
accounts.hypothesis: Capital-structure change plus global manufacturing and future M&A can create finance-standardization, consolidation and planning requirements.
accounts.first_move: Treat as a research target only after confirming size and ERP architecture; approach through sponsor / finance transformation if mid-market scope exists.
accounts.gaps: Revenue scale, current ERP, global entity complexity, sponsor priorities, NetSuite fit versus enterprise ERP.

accounts.why_now: Entered a definitive agreement to be acquired by H.I.G. Capital in an approximately $866M enterprise-value take-private.
accounts.hypothesis: Take-private transactions can trigger reporting redesign, carve-out / integration decisions and sponsor-led technology reviews, but company scale may push beyond the core NetSuite sweet spot.
accounts.first_move: Qualify fit through Baker Tilly transaction / PE relationships before any ERP outreach.
accounts.gaps: ERP landscape, sponsor plan, company size versus NetSuite fit, TSA / integration needs, existing Baker Tilly relationship.

accounts.why_now: Appointed J. Michael Bruff as CFO effective October 5, 2026, with a mandate framed around transformation, growth and value creation.
accounts.hypothesis: New finance leadership is a useful research signal, though Presidio's scale may make NetSuite a poor fit for core ERP. The correct move is qualify, not force the account.
accounts.first_move: Use as an example of why Account IQ includes fit and disqualification: new CFO alone is not enough.
accounts.gaps: Current enterprise ERP, subsidiary use cases, two-tier ERP potential, Baker Tilly relationship.
